ECE 6390 / Digital signals

Compression vs coding

From the figure to the physics

Fig. 1 shows the different roles of compression, error correction and modulation.

Source entropy H = −Σpᵢlog₂pᵢ describes average information per source symbol for a stated probability model. A variable-length lossless code can use shorter codewords for more likely symbols.

Average code length is L̄ = Σpᵢlᵢ. Multiplying by source-symbol rate gives the compressed bit rate. A channel code of rate Rc then increases the transmitted coded-bit rate to Rcompressed/Rc.

Compression exploits source redundancy, while error-correcting coding adds structured redundancy for recovery over a channel. Modulation maps the resulting bits onto transmitted symbols. Lossy compression introduces another deliberate information trade.

Example

For probabilities 1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 1/8, code lengths 1, 2, 3, 3 average 1.75 bits per source symbol, compared with 2 for a fixed-length code.

Model and course sources

    Practice

    1. A compressed stream carries 1.75 Mbit/s. What coded rate follows a rate-1/2 channel encoder?

    Code rate is information bits divided by coded bits.

    The coded stream is 1.75/(1/2) = 3.5 Mbit/s. This added redundancy serves transmission reliability rather than source compression.
